title: AP2 v0.2 actors and trust boundaries
caption: Five roles in four trust zones. The Trusted Surface must be non-agentic and holds the user's signing key; the Shopping Agent is treated as a potential attacker; merchant and payment parties verify mandates in deterministic code. Catalog and checkout messages belong to the surrounding commerce protocol.
alt: Flowchart. The user zone holds the user and the Trusted Surface with user_sk; the user gives consent to the surface. The agent zone holds the Shopping Agent with its key in cnf. The agent sends Mandate Content to the Trusted Surface and gets signed mandates back. The agent shops through a commerce protocol such as UCP or A2A, which talks to the Merchant. The agent sends the Payment Mandate to the Credential Provider, which may ask the Network for a scoped credential and returns a token. The agent sends the token and the Checkout Mandate to the Merchant, which sends the token and the checkout_jwt hash to the Merchant Payment Processor. The processor returns a Payment Receipt and the Merchant a Checkout Receipt to the agent.
